description: The physics of electric and magnetic fields and their interactions with matter. Covers electrostatics, magnetostatics, electromagnetic induction, Maxwell's equations, and electromagnetic waves.

concepts.title: Coulomb's Law and the Electric Field
learning_objectives: State Coulomb's law and compute the force between point charges
Define the electric field E as force per unit charge and compute it for point charge configurations
Apply the principle of superposition to find E for discrete charge distributions

concepts.title: Continuous Charge Distributions
learning_objectives: Compute the electric field from continuous line, surface, and volume charge distributions using integration
Set up and evaluate integrals for E from symmetric charge distributions (ring, disk, rod)
Apply symmetry arguments to simplify electric field calculations

concepts.title: Gauss's Law
learning_objectives: State Gauss's law in integral form: ∮ E·dA = Q_enc/ε₀
Apply Gauss's law to calculate electric fields for systems with high symmetry (sphere, cylinder, plane)
Relate Gauss's law to the divergence theorem and state the differential form ∇·E = ρ/ε₀

concepts.title: Electric Potential
learning_objectives: Define electric potential V as the line integral of E and compute V for point charges and continuous distributions
Relate E to V via E = −∇V
Calculate potential differences and work done moving charges in electric fields

concepts.title: Electrostatic Energy
learning_objectives: Compute the energy stored in a charge configuration using U = ½ Σ qᵢVᵢ
Derive the energy density of the electric field: u = ½ε₀E²
Calculate the total electrostatic energy by integrating the energy density

concepts.title: Conductors in Electrostatic Equilibrium
learning_objectives: Explain why E = 0 inside a conductor and charge resides on the surface
Determine surface charge distributions on conductors using boundary conditions
Analyze the method of images for a point charge near a grounded conducting plane

concepts.title: Capacitance and Dielectrics
learning_objectives: Define capacitance C = Q/V and calculate it for parallel plate, cylindrical, and spherical capacitors
Calculate the energy stored in a capacitor: U = ½CV²
Analyze the effect of dielectric materials on capacitance and field using ε = κε₀

concepts.title: Laplace's and Poisson's Equations
learning_objectives: Derive Poisson's equation ∇²V = −ρ/ε₀ and Laplace's equation ∇²V = 0
Solve Laplace's equation in Cartesian and spherical coordinates for simple boundary conditions
Apply uniqueness theorems to electrostatic boundary value problems

concepts.title: Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law
learning_objectives: Define current density J and relate it to charge carrier drift velocity
State Ohm's law in microscopic form J = σE and macroscopic form V = IR
Calculate resistance from resistivity and geometry

concepts.title: DC Circuit Analysis
learning_objectives: Apply Kirchhoff's junction and loop rules to analyze multi-loop circuits
Analyze series and parallel combinations of resistors and capacitors
Solve RC circuit transient problems using first-order ODEs

concepts.title: Magnetic Force and the Lorentz Force Law
learning_objectives: State the Lorentz force law F = q(E + v × B) and compute magnetic forces on moving charges
Analyze the motion of charged particles in uniform magnetic fields (cyclotron motion)
Compute the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field

concepts.title: Sources of Magnetic Fields: Biot-Savart Law
learning_objectives: State the Biot-Savart law dB = (μ₀/4π)(Idl × r̂)/r²
Compute the magnetic field from a straight wire, a circular loop, and a solenoid using Biot-Savart
Apply superposition to find B from combinations of current-carrying elements

concepts.title: Ampere's Law
learning_objectives: State Ampere's law in integral form: ∮ B·dl = μ₀I_enc
Apply Ampere's law to compute B for systems with high symmetry (solenoid, toroid, coaxial cable)
State the differential form ∇ × B = μ₀J and relate it to Stokes' theorem

concepts.title: Magnetic Dipoles and Magnetization
learning_objectives: Define the magnetic dipole moment m = IA for a current loop
Compute torque and potential energy of a magnetic dipole in an external field
Classify magnetic materials as diamagnetic, paramagnetic, or ferromagnetic

concepts.title: Faraday's Law of Induction
learning_objectives: State Faraday's law: EMF = −dΦ_B/dt and compute magnetic flux through surfaces
Apply Faraday's law to calculate induced EMF in loops and coils
Apply Lenz's law to determine the direction of induced current

concepts.title: Inductance and RL Circuits
learning_objectives: Define self-inductance L and compute it for solenoids and toroids
Define mutual inductance and compute it for simple coupled circuits
Solve RL circuit transient problems and compute energy stored in an inductor: U = ½LI²

concepts.title: Motional EMF and Eddy Currents
learning_objectives: Compute motional EMF from F = qv × B for a conductor moving through a magnetic field
Analyze generators and alternators using Faraday's law
Explain eddy currents and their role in braking and heating

concepts.title: AC Sources, Phasors, and Impedance
learning_objectives: Represent AC voltages and currents as phasors (complex exponentials)
Define impedance Z for resistors, capacitors, and inductors
Analyze series and parallel RLC circuits using complex impedance

concepts.title: Power in AC Circuits and Resonance
learning_objectives: Calculate average power, reactive power, and power factor in AC circuits
Analyze series and parallel RLC resonance: resonant frequency, bandwidth, quality factor
Design filters (low-pass, high-pass, band-pass) using RLC combinations

concepts.title: Displacement Current and Maxwell's Correction
learning_objectives: Identify the inconsistency in Ampere's law for time-varying fields
Derive Maxwell's displacement current term J_d = ε₀ ∂E/∂t
Write the complete Ampere-Maxwell law: ∇ × B = μ₀J + μ₀ε₀ ∂E/∂t

concepts.title: Maxwell's Equations in Differential and Integral Form
learning_objectives: State all four Maxwell's equations in both differential and integral form
Identify the physical content and experimental basis of each equation
Apply boundary conditions for E and B at interfaces between media

concepts.title: The Electromagnetic Wave Equation
learning_objectives: Derive the wave equation for E and B from Maxwell's equations in free space
Identify the speed of electromagnetic waves as c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀)
Write plane wave solutions and identify wavelength, frequency, and polarization

concepts.title: Properties of Electromagnetic Waves
learning_objectives: Show that E and B in a plane wave are perpendicular to each other and to the propagation direction
Relate E and B amplitudes via E₀ = cB₀
Describe the electromagnetic spectrum and identify regions by wavelength and frequency

concepts.title: Energy and Momentum in Electromagnetic Waves
learning_objectives: Derive the Poynting vector S = (1/μ₀)(E × B) and interpret it as energy flux
Compute the intensity of an electromagnetic wave as the time-averaged Poynting vector
Calculate radiation pressure and the momentum carried by electromagnetic waves

concepts.title: Polarization
learning_objectives: Describe linear, circular, and elliptical polarization of electromagnetic waves
Apply Malus's law to compute intensity through polarizing filters
Analyze polarization using Jones vectors and Jones matrices

concepts.title: Reflection and Refraction
learning_objectives: Derive the laws of reflection and refraction (Snell's law) from boundary conditions on E and B
Derive the Fresnel equations for reflection and transmission amplitudes
Compute reflectance and transmittance at dielectric interfaces

concepts.title: Dispersion and Absorption
learning_objectives: Model the frequency-dependent dielectric constant using the Lorentz oscillator model
Distinguish between phase velocity and group velocity in dispersive media
Analyze anomalous dispersion and absorption near resonance frequencies

concepts.title: Retarded Potentials
learning_objectives: Define the retarded potentials V(r,t) and A(r,t) accounting for the finite speed of light
Explain the physical significance of retarded time t_r = t − |r−r'|/c
Compute retarded potentials for simple time-varying source configurations

concepts.title: Radiation from Accelerating Charges
learning_objectives: Derive the Larmor formula for radiated power from an accelerating point charge
Describe the radiation pattern of an oscillating electric dipole
Compute radiated power and radiation resistance for a short dipole antenna

concepts.title: Radiation Reaction and the Abraham-Lorentz Force
learning_objectives: Derive the Abraham-Lorentz formula for radiation reaction force
Identify the problems of runaway solutions and preacceleration
Discuss the limitations of classical electrodynamics for radiating charges

projects.title: Designing an LC Band-Pass Filter
projects.description: Design, analyze, and simulate a band-pass filter for a target frequency range. Compute the transfer function, plot the frequency response, and determine the quality factor and bandwidth.
learning_objectives: Apply complex impedance analysis to a multi-component circuit
Derive and plot the frequency response (Bode plot) of a filter
Relate quality factor to bandwidth and component values

projects.title: Deriving the Radiation Pattern of a Half-Wave Antenna
projects.description: Compute the radiation pattern of a half-wave dipole antenna by integrating contributions from each infinitesimal current element using retarded potentials.
learning_objectives: Set up the retarded potential integral for a current distribution
Evaluate the far-field approximation to obtain the radiation pattern
Plot the radiation pattern and compute the directivity

projects.title: Verifying Maxwell's Equations for a Charging Capacitor
projects.description: Analyze a parallel-plate capacitor being charged by a current. Show that the displacement current between the plates equals the conduction current in the wire, and verify all four Maxwell's equations for this system.
learning_objectives: Compute the time-varying electric field between capacitor plates
Calculate the displacement current and verify it equals the conduction current
Apply Ampere-Maxwell law to compute the magnetic field between the plates
